subject: History
description: Covers Champaran, Kheda, Ahmedabad, Non-Cooperation, Dandi March, and Quit India.

questions.stem: Mahatma Gandhi's first major public appearance after returning to India from South Africa was at the inauguration of which institution in 1916?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: After returning to India in 1915, Gandhi spent a year travelling the country on the advice of his political guru, Gopal Krishna Gokhale. His first major public address was at the opening of the Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in February 1916. He shocked the elite audience of princes and viceroys by criticizing them for their ostentatious wealth while millions of Indians lived in grinding poverty.
DECOY BUSTING: The Lucknow Session of the INC happened later in December 1916 (where he met Rajkumar Shukla, leading to Champaran). AMU was founded by Syed Ahmad Khan in 1875. Visva-Bharati was founded by Tagore.
EXAM INSIGHT: This speech at BHU marked Gandhi's emergence from the shadows. He boldly declared that there is no salvation for India unless the elite strip themselves of their jewelry and hold it in trust for the countrymen. It clearly signaled his intention to turn the freedom struggle from an elite club into a mass movement.

questions.stem: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, Gandhi's first civil disobedience movement in India, was organized to protest against the:

options.option_text: Tinkathia system, which forced farmers to grow indigo on 3/20th of their land
Oppressive land revenue taxes imposed during a severe drought
Dispute between mill owners and workers over the Plague Bonus
Passage of the draconian Rowlatt Act

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: In Champaran (Bihar), European planters forced local peasants to grow indigo (a cash crop used for blue dye) on 3/20th of their land holdings under an exploitative system known as the 'Tinkathia' system. When synthetic dyes ruined the indigo market, planters demanded heavy compensation to free the peasants from this obligation. Gandhi's intervention successfully dismantled the Tinkathia system.
DECOY BUSTING: 
- Oppressive taxes during drought = Kheda Satyagraha (1918, First Non-Cooperation).
- Dispute over Plague Bonus = Ahmedabad Mill Strike (1918, First Hunger Strike).
- Rowlatt Act = Rowlatt Satyagraha (1919, first all-India mass strike).
EXAM INSIGHT: Champaran is historically significant as the FIRST successful application of Satyagraha (truth-force/non-violent resistance) on Indian soil. Gandhi was invited to Champaran by a persistent local peasant named Rajkumar Shukla.

questions.stem: During which movement did Mahatma Gandhi use the tactic of a 'Hunger Strike' (fast unto death) for the very first time in India?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: In 1918, a dispute broke out between the textile mill owners and workers of Ahmedabad regarding the withdrawal of a 'Plague Bonus'. The workers demanded a 50% wage hike, while owners offered 20%. Gandhi intervened, asked workers to strike and demand 35%, and undertook his FIRST fast unto death (hunger strike) to strengthen the workers' resolve. The pressure worked, and the owners agreed to the 35% hike.
DECOY BUSTING: Champaran was his first Civil Disobedience. Kheda was his first Non-Cooperation. The 1920 Non-Cooperation Movement was his first nationwide mass movement. 
EXAM INSIGHT: Memorize the chronological triad of Gandhi's early regional experiments: Champaran (1917 - Civil Disobedience) -> Ahmedabad Mill Strike (Feb 1918 - Hunger Strike) -> Kheda (Mar 1918 - Non-Cooperation). These three built his reputation as a leader of the masses.

questions.stem: Why did Mahatma Gandhi abruptly call off the nationwide Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922?

options.option_text: Due to a violent mob incident in Chauri Chaura where 22 policemen were burnt alive
Due to the signing of the Gandhi-Irwin Pact
Because the British Government agreed to grant Dominion Status to India
Following the arrest and deportation of prominent leaders like Bal Gangadhar Tilak

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Non-Cooperation Movement was peaking in 1922. However, on February 5, 1922, a peaceful protest at Chauri Chaura (Gorakhpur, UP) turned violent when police opened fire. The angry mob chased the police into the station and set it on fire, killing 22 policemen. Gandhi, an absolute purist regarding non-violence (Ahimsa), was deeply shocked. He immediately halted the movement, realizing the masses were not yet ready for strictly non-violent Satyagraha.
DECOY BUSTING: The Gandhi-Irwin pact (1931) halted the later Civil Disobedience Movement, not Non-Cooperation. The British did not offer Dominion status in 1922 (that came much later).
EXAM INSIGHT: The abrupt withdrawal deeply disillusioned young revolutionaries (leading to the rise of Bhagat Singh and the HRA) and political leaders like C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru, who broke away to form the Swaraj Party to fight the British from inside the legislative councils.

questions.stem: The historic Dandi March (Salt March) of 1930 marked the beginning of which major phase of the Indian freedom struggle?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Gandhi chose to attack the oppressive British monopoly and tax on Salt—a basic necessity for the poorest of the poor—as a brilliant unifying symbol. He marched 240 miles from Sabarmati Ashram to the coastal village of Dandi. On April 6, 1930, he picked up a lump of salt, technically breaking the salt law. This act of breaking a specific British law was the formal launch of the Civil Disobedience Movement across the country.
DECOY BUSTING: Non-Cooperation (1920) was about boycotting British institutions (schools, courts, foreign cloth) but not explicitly breaking laws. Quit India (1942) was the final push demanding immediate British withdrawal. Swadeshi (1905) was an economic boycott post-Bengal partition, before Gandhi's era.
EXAM INSIGHT: The Dandi March garnered massive international press coverage, turning the Indian independence struggle into a global moral issue. It also saw the massive participation of women (like Sarojini Naidu) who stepped out of their homes to break the salt laws.

questions.stem: In 1932, Mahatma Gandhi went on a fast unto death in the Yerwada Jail to protest against:

options.option_text: The Communal Award announced by Ramsay MacDonald, which granted separate electorates to the Depressed Classes (Dalits)
The execution of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru
The failure of the Second Round Table Conference to grant Dominion Status
The brutal suppression of the Quit India movement by the British police

questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: In 1932, British PM Ramsay MacDonald announced the 'Communal Award', extending the divisive "separate electorates" (where only Dalits could vote for Dalit candidates) to the Depressed Classes. B.R. Ambedkar supported this for Dalit political empowerment. Gandhi opposed it vehemently, fearing it would permanently divide Hindu society and cripple the untouchability eradication movement. He began a fast unto death in Yerwada jail to protest.
DECOY BUSTING: The execution of Bhagat Singh (1931) happened before the Gandhi-Irwin pact. The Quit India movement happened a decade later in 1942.
EXAM INSIGHT: The fast led to massive public pressure, resulting in the Poona Pact (1932) signed between B.R. Ambedkar and Gandhi's representatives. The pact abandoned separate electorates but massively increased the number of seats RESERVED for the Depressed Classes within the general electorate. It was a historic compromise.

questions.stem: During the Quit India Movement in 1942, Mahatma Gandhi gave the famous slogan 'Do or Die'. At which historic ground in Mumbai was this speech delivered?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: On August 8, 1942, at the Bombay session of the All-India Congress Committee held at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Gandhi launched the Quit India Movement. He delivered his electrifying speech, giving the mantra "Do or Die" (Karo ya Maro): "We shall either free India or die in the attempt; we shall not live to see the perpetuation of our slavery."
DECOY BUSTING: Azad Maidan, Shivaji Park, and Cross Maidan are famous grounds in Mumbai, but Gowalia Tank is the specific location of the Quit India resolution.
EXAM INSIGHT: Because of this historic event, Gowalia Tank Maidan was officially renamed August Kranti Maidan. The very next morning (August 9), the British arrested the entire Congress leadership in a sweep (Operation Zero Hour), leaving the Quit India movement to be a spontaneous, leaderless, and often violent mass uprising.
